rows.name: DICE_ADMIN_GROUP
rows.who_sets: A person, in the environment of the Dice daemon.
rows.values: The name of a Unix group. A name that does not exist gives no extra rights and no error.
rows.default: Unset: only root and the user that runs the daemon are Dice administrators.
rows.effect: Members of the group become Dice administrators. An administrator can cancel the submissions (commands that Dice queues or runs) of other users, attach to them and see their full details. An administrator can also stop the daemon.
rows.notes: The daemon reads its own environment at each request. A value in the environment of a client has no effect. The daemon takes the user id of the client from the socket. The packaged `dice.service` does not set the variable.

rows.name: DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG
rows.who_sets: The test fixtures of Dice and Slice.
rows.read_by: `dice`, `slice` and the wrappers (`bin/dice`, `bin/slice`, `bin/rinzler` and 1 more file)
rows.values: Exactly `1` allows the override. Any other text does not.
rows.default: Unset: a set `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH` is an error in `bin/dice`, `bin/slice` and the wrappers. The error contains `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH is test-only`.
rows.effect: Gives the permission that `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH` needs. That variable replaces `/etc/positron/dice.yaml` (the Dice host configuration file) with a test file. Without that variable, `DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG` changes nothing.
rows.notes: The override needs `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` and a Git checkout. Pytest must be the process or one of its 5 nearest ancestors. `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_SPAWN_OK` gives one exception. A shared host needs `DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_SHADOW_SHARED`. Outside an override, the Dice daemon removes it from the environment of the programs it starts.

rows.name: DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_SHADOW_SHARED
rows.who_sets: The test fixtures of Dice and Slice.
rows.read_by: `dice`, `slice` and the wrappers (`bin/dice`, `bin/slice`, `bin/rinzler` and 1 more file)
rows.values: Exactly `1` enables it. Any other text is off.
rows.default: Unset: on a shared host, `bin/dice` rejects a `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH` that names another file than `/etc/positron/dice.yaml`.
rows.effect: Lets `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH` replace the Dice host configuration file on a shared host (a server whose `/etc/positron/dice.yaml` sets `mode: shared`).
rows.notes: The error contains `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH is disabled`. `DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG` must also be `1`. When `bin/dice` is missing, `bin/slice` and the wrappers ignore the override and print no such error. The Dice daemon does not remove this variable from the environment of the programs it starts.

rows.name: DICE_ALLOW_TEST_RUNNER
rows.who_sets: The tests of the LSF bridge in `bin/slice-tests`.
rows.values: Exactly `1` enables it. Any other text is off.
rows.default: Unset: the hidden option `--runner` must name the `bin/dice-lsf-runner` of the same checkout.
rows.effect: Lets `bin/dice-lsf-submit` (the script that submits a Dice job to LSF) accept a `--runner` path that is not the `bin/dice-lsf-runner` beside it.
rows.notes: Without it, another `--runner` path ends the script with the error `--runner is reserved for bridge tests` and exit status 2.

evidence.quote: parser.error("--runner is reserved for bridge tests")

rows.name: DICE_BOX_SLOTS
rows.who_sets: A person, in the environment of the Dice daemon or `bin/slice`.
rows.values: Integer greater than 0, parsed with `int()`. Other text, `0` or a negative number ends the program with an error.
rows.default: Unset: `SLICE_BOX_CAPACITY` is used. If that is also unset, the count comes from `config/resource-map.yaml`.
rows.effect: Sets the number of slots of the server. The Dice daemon schedules over that many slots. `bin/slice` uses it as the total slot count.
rows.notes: The daemon reads it once at startup. The daemon option `--box` takes priority. The packaged `dice.service` sets neither. On a shared host `bin/slice` first asks the running daemon for the count. It reads the variable only when that fails or when `DICE_DISABLE` is `1`.

evidence.quote: raise SystemExit(f"dice: invalid box capacity {n} — must be a positive integer")
self.box: int = box if box is not None else _discover_box()

rows.name: DICE_CANCEL_SIGKILL_SEC
rows.who_sets: A person, in the environment of the Dice daemon.
rows.values: Number of seconds, parsed with `float()`. Text that is not a number ends the daemon at startup with an error.
rows.default: Unset: 10 seconds. Empty: the daemon ends at startup with the error `DICE_CANCEL_SIGKILL_SEC must be a number`.
rows.effect: Sets how long the Dice daemon waits before it sends `SIGKILL` to a cancelled submission that is still running. The wait starts at the first cancel request.
rows.notes: Read once at startup. `0`, a negative number, `inf` or `nan` gives 10 seconds. A cancel from an LSF runner or after a lost lease waits at most 2 seconds. The wait also applies when the first process of a submission exits and others remain.

evidence.quote: raise SystemExit("dice: DICE_CANCEL_SIGKILL_SEC must be a number")
self._cancel_sigkill_after = grace if grace > 0 and math.isfinite(grace) else 10.0

rows.name: DICE_DAEMON_CHILD
rows.who_sets: The Dice daemon. `bin/slice` passes it to child tests.
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, `rinzler_proxy`, the wrappers and `slice` (`src/system/system.cpp`, `bin/rinzler`, `bin/slice` and 2 more files)
rows.values: Exactly `1` means that the Dice daemon started the process. Any other text counts as unset. The text is compared, not parsed as a number.
rows.default: Unset: the process is not under a Dice grant. `rinzler` and `runtron` parse placement options without grant checks.
rows.effect: `rinzler` and `runtron` check placement options such as `--instance`, `--devices` and `--numa` against the granted slots. They then need `DICE_SLOTS`, `DICE_GRANT_ID`, `DICE_GRANT_TOKEN` and a `SYSTEM_CONFIG` with `--instance`. With `DICE_SLOTS` on a shared host, the wrappers and `bin/slice` start the work without a new submission.
rows.notes: Set by hand without a complete grant, it makes `rinzler` and `runtron` fail at startup. Under a grant, `--no-opt` does not stop the pinning of application threads to the granted cores. On a legacy host the wrappers remove it before they start `gen/rinzler` or `gen/runtron`.

rows.name: DICE_DISABLE
rows.who_sets: A person, by hand. The Slice test fixtures also set it.
rows.read_by: `dice`, `slice` and the wrappers (`bin/dice`, `bin/slice`, `bin/rinzler` and 1 more file)
rows.values: Exactly `1` enables it. Any other text, for example `true`, is off.
rows.default: Unset: off. The Dice host configuration file `/etc/positron/dice.yaml` decides whether work goes through Dice.
rows.effect: On a legacy host the wrappers and `bin/slice` start the work directly, with or without the variable. On a shared host the wrappers and `slice run`, `slice bench`, `slice calibrate` and `slice submit` refuse to run and exit with status 2.
rows.notes: On every host the `bin/dice` commands `daemon`, `submit`, `queue` and `cancel` fail with exit status 1. With `--remote`, the wrappers and `bin/slice` exit with status 2 unless `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`. Outside tests, the Dice daemon removes it from the environment of the programs it starts.

evidence.quote: "error: DICE_DISABLE=1 is not permitted on a shared Dice host",
raise RuntimeError("DICE_DISABLE=1 — direct dice commands are disabled")

rows.name: DICE_ETA
rows.values: Seconds as a number of 0 or more, or `inf`, `infinity`, `infty`, or `?` for no estimate. A negative number or other text makes `slice submit` exit with status 2.
rows.default: Unset: `inf`. Dice then expects no end time for the submission.
rows.effect: Sets the predicted run time that the wrapper passes as `--eta` to `bin/slice submit` when it queues `rinzler` or `runtron` through Dice. The Dice scheduler uses the value to decide whether a later submission can start before an earlier one.
rows.notes: The wrapper reads it only on a shared host outside a grant. Dice does not stop a submission that runs longer. `bin/dice-lsf-runner` removes every `DICE_` variable from remote work. A value from the submitting shell does not reach a `--remote` run.

evidence.quote: raise ValueError(f"eta must be non-negative; got {v}")

rows.name: DICE_GRANT_ID
rows.who_sets: The Dice daemon. `bin/slice` passes it to child tests.
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, `rinzler_proxy`, the wrappers and `slice` (`src/system/system.cpp`, `bin/rinzler`, `bin/slice` and 2 more files)
rows.values: Text that is not empty. It is the id of a Dice submission, for example `sub-2026-11-21-003`. The readers do not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: `rinzler` and `runtron` do not read it unless `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` is `1`. In that case they fail at startup with `Incomplete Dice grant environment`.
rows.effect: Names the grant (the slots that Dice gave to one submission). `rinzler` and `runtron` keep their computed placement while this id and the slot list stay the same. The wrappers and `bin/slice` send it to the daemon with `DICE_GRANT_TOKEN` to confirm the grant.
rows.notes: `rinzler` and `runtron` print it in `Dice grant <id>:` error lines. On a shared host the wrappers and `bin/slice` exit with status 2 when `DICE_SLOTS` and `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` are set but the id is missing. `bin/ci/bench_refresh_quiesce.py` compares it with the id of the running submission.

evidence.quote: spdlog::error("Incomplete Dice grant environment; launch through Dice again");
if (dice_placement.identity == identity && dice_placement.slots == slots) return true;

rows.name: DICE_GRANT_TOKEN
rows.who_sets: The Dice daemon. `bin/slice` passes it to child tests.
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `runtron`, `rinzler_proxy`, the wrappers and `slice` (`src/system/system.cpp`, `bin/rinzler`, `bin/slice` and 1 more file)
rows.values: Text that is not empty. It is random text that the Dice daemon creates for one grant. The readers do not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: `rinzler` and `runtron` do not read it unless `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` is `1`. In that case they fail at startup with `Incomplete Dice grant environment`.
rows.effect: Proves the grant to the Dice daemon. The wrappers and `bin/slice` send it with `DICE_GRANT_ID` in a `grant-check` request, and the daemon compares it with the stored token. `rinzler` and `runtron` only test that it is set and not empty.
rows.notes: `bin/slice` leaves it out of the command line that it writes to test logs. The daemon accepts the check only from the started program, its process group or its descendants. Without it, the wrappers and `bin/slice` exit with status 2 inside a grant.

rows.name: DICE_LABEL
rows.who_sets: A person, `slice submit`, or the Dice daemon.
rows.values: Any text. Spaces around the text are removed. Text that is empty after that counts as unset.
rows.default: Unset: the label is `make <goals>` when `MAKECMDGOALS` is set. Otherwise `bin/slice` builds a label from its arguments or sends none.
rows.effect: Sets the label of the submissions that `slice run`, `slice bench` and `slice submit` send to Dice. The Dice queue shows the label. `slice run` also records it in its state file.
rows.notes: The option `--label` of `slice submit` takes priority. The wrappers always pass `--label`, and the variable does not change their label. `slice submit` and the Dice daemon also set it for the program that Dice starts.

rows.name: DICE_LOCK_PATH
rows.values: A file path. The text is used as given.
rows.default: Unset: `dice.lock` in the Dice runtime directory. That directory is `/run/dice` on a shared host.
rows.effect: Moves the lock file that the Dice daemon holds while it runs. A second daemon that uses the same lock file does not start.
rows.notes: Only tests can use it. On a shared host outside a `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH` override, a daemon with this variable does not start. It prints `DICE_LOCK_PATH is test-only in shared Dice`. A client ignores the variable there. On a legacy host no Dice daemon runs.

evidence.quote: return Path(override) if override else runtime_dir() / _LOCK_FILE_NAME
f"{name} is test-only in shared Dice; use "

rows.name: DICE_LOG_DIR
rows.values: A directory path. The text is used as given.
rows.default: Unset: the directory `logs` in the Dice runtime directory. That directory is `/run/dice` on a shared host.
rows.effect: Moves the directory where the Dice daemon writes one log file for each submission. The file name is `<id>.log`. The daemon sends the file path to a client that attaches.
rows.notes: Only tests can use it. On a shared host outside a `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH` override, a daemon with this variable does not start. It prints `DICE_LOG_DIR is test-only in shared Dice`. A client ignores the variable there. On a legacy host no Dice daemon runs.

evidence.quote: return Path(override) if override else runtime_dir() / "logs"
f"{name} is test-only in shared Dice; use "

rows.name: DICE_LOG_PATH
rows.values: A file path. The text is used as given.
rows.default: Unset: `dice.log` in the Dice runtime directory. That directory is `/run/dice` on a shared host.
rows.effect: Moves the log file of the Dice daemon.
rows.notes: Only tests can use it. On a shared host outside a `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH` override, a daemon with this variable does not start. It prints `DICE_LOG_PATH is test-only in shared Dice`. A client ignores the variable there. On a legacy host no Dice daemon runs.

evidence.quote: return Path(override) if override else runtime_dir() / "dice.log"
f"{name} is test-only in shared Dice; use "

rows.name: DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID
rows.read_by: `dice` daemon (`bin/dice`). It takes the name from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment.
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `int()`. It is the process id of the LSF runner (`bin/dice-lsf-runner`, the script that an LSF job runs on the FPGA server).
rows.default: Unset: with `DICE_LSF_LEASE_START_JIFFIES` also unset, the submission has no runner lease. Empty: the daemon rejects the submit request.
rows.effect: On a shared host the Dice daemon records the runner process as the owner of the submission. When that process is gone, the daemon cancels the submission. It sends `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after at most 2 seconds.
rows.notes: When either lease variable is set, the daemon rejects the request unless both are integers, `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`, the pair matches a live process of the same user, and the client descends from that process. `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1` without the two lease variables is also rejected.

rows.name: DICE_LSF_LEASE_START_JIFFIES
rows.read_by: `dice` daemon (`bin/dice`). It takes the name from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment.
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `int()`. It is the start time of the LSF runner process in clock ticks counted from boot, from field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`.
rows.default: Unset: with `DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID` also unset, the submission has no runner lease. Empty: the daemon rejects the submit request.
rows.effect: Together with `DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID` it identifies the LSF runner process that owns the submission. The Dice daemon compares it with the start time of that process id. A different start time counts as a lost lease, and the daemon cancels the submission.
rows.notes: The daemon rejects a request with only one lease variable, with text that is not an integer, or without `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1`. A value of 0 clock ticks or less never matches a live process. The runner sets both only after it reads its own start time.

new_terms.definition: One command that a client asks the Dice daemon to run on a number of slots. The daemon queues it, then starts it.
The slots that the Dice daemon gives to one submission while it runs.
A server whose `/etc/positron/dice.yaml` sets `mode: shared`. A Dice daemon queues the FPGA work of all users there.
A server whose `/etc/positron/dice.yaml` is missing or does not set `mode: shared`. No Dice daemon runs there. The wrappers and Slice start work directly.
The launcher scripts `bin/rinzler` and `bin/runtron`. On a shared host they start `gen/rinzler` and `gen/runtron` through Dice. On a legacy host they start them directly.
The directory that holds the socket, state, lock and log files of the Dice daemon. It is `/run/dice` on a shared host.
`bin/dice-lsf-runner`, the script that an LSF job runs on the FPGA server. It starts the work through the Dice daemon of that server.
The process id and the start time of an LSF runner. The Dice daemon records them as the owner of a submission. It cancels the submission when that process is gone.

A user who may cancel, attach to and inspect the submissions of other users, and stop the Dice daemon. Root and the user that runs the daemon are administrators. `DICE_ADMIN_GROUP` adds one Unix group.
`bin/dice-lsf-submit`. It writes a job description and submits it to LSF. The LSF job then runs the LSF runner on an FPGA server.

notes: All 17 names are environment variables in scope. None is dropped. Every evidence quote was opened again and equals its source line. Checked facts that stay as written: `--box` has priority over DICE_BOX_SLOTS (bin/dice:1935), against doc/dice.md:586. DICE_DISABLE=1 changes no routing on a legacy host and is refused on a shared host (bin/rinzler:137-147, bin/slice:5159-5165). The Dice daemon starts only when the host configuration selects shared mode (bin/dice:4349), and DICE_LOCK_PATH, DICE_LOG_DIR and DICE_LOG_PATH are refused there outside the pytest override (bin/dice:397), so the three rows stay in group dice-test-hooks. Corrections: (1) the three path rows said `bin/dice` fails. Only the daemon fails at startup. A client does not read the names on a host that runs dice.service. (2) DICE_CANCEL_SIGKILL_SEC also sets the wait after the first process of a submission exits while other processes of it remain. (3) The two lease rows gave 'no runner lease' as the unset behaviour. That holds only when both lease names are unset. (4) DICE_GRANT_TOKEN alone does not pass the grant check. The daemon also tests the calling process. (5) Error texts are printed after a prefix (`dice: ` or `error: `), so 'starts with' became 'contains'. (6) DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG has one exception to the pytest ancestor rule (DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_SPAWN_OK). Group choices to review: DICE_LABEL is read only by bin/slice but stays in group dice. It labels Dice submissions, and the daemon sets it. DICE_ETA is in group wrappers. DICE_ALLOW_TEST_RUNNER is in dice-test-hooks although its reader is the LSF submit script. The rows use the terms in new_terms without a definition in every cell. The word limits do not leave room for that. The document needs these terms in its glossary. Test gap: no test sets DICE_ADMIN_GROUP to a group name. bin/dice-tests/test_integration.py:591 and :811 only remove it, so the group branch at bin/dice:2824-2831 is read from the code only. read_by of the three grant rows names `rinzler`, `runtron` and `rinzler_proxy`. `rinzler_mock` and `rinzler_host` compile the same src/rinzler.cpp (src/CMakeLists.txt:115, src/CMakeLists.txt:152) and read the names too. They are left out because the glossary does not define them. Not covered for lack of room: with DICE_DISABLE=1, `slice attach`, `slice cancel`, `slice daemon start` and `slice daemon stop` print a refusal and exit with status 1 (bin/slice:5921, bin/slice:6199, bin/slice:6279, bin/slice:6303).

changes.name: DICE_GRANT_TOKEN
changes.was: Proves the grant to the Dice daemon. The wrappers and `bin/slice` send it with `DICE_GRANT_ID` in a `grant-check` request, and the daemon compares it with the stored token. `rinzler` and `runtron` only test that it is present.
changes.now: Proves the grant to the Dice daemon. The wrappers and `bin/slice` send it with `DICE_GRANT_ID` in a `grant-check` request, and the daemon compares it with the stored token. `rinzler` and `runtron` only test that it is set and not empty.
changes.why: The C++ test is 'not null and first character not NUL' (src/system/system.cpp:131-133). 'Present' did not say that an empty value fails.

changes.name: DICE_GRANT_TOKEN
changes.was: It is a secret. `bin/slice` leaves it out of the command line that it writes to test logs. On a shared host the wrappers and `bin/slice` exit with status 2 when `DICE_SLOTS` and `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` are set but the token is missing.
changes.now: `bin/slice` leaves it out of the command line that it writes to test logs. The daemon accepts the check only from the started program, its process group or its descendants. Without it, the wrappers and `bin/slice` exit with status 2 inside a grant.
changes.why: The row implied that the token alone proves the grant. In shared mode the daemon also requires that the caller is the granted process, a member of its process group, or a descendant (bin/dice:3125, bin/dice:2839-2856). A token copied to another shell does not pass. 'It is a secret' was removed to make room: the log rule states the same fact from the code (bin/slice:1724-1726).

changes.name: DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID
changes.was: `dice` daemon, from the environment that a client sends with a submit request (`bin/dice`)
changes.now: `dice` daemon (`bin/dice`). It takes the name from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment.
changes.why: Same fact, in the read_by format (program, then file). The lookup is in the `env` field of the submit request (bin/dice:2963, bin/dice:2977-2981).

changes.name: DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID
changes.was: Unset: the submission has no runner lease. Empty: the daemon rejects the submit request.
changes.now: Unset: with `DICE_LSF_LEASE_START_JIFFIES` also unset, the submission has no runner lease. Empty: the daemon rejects the submit request.
changes.why: 'Unset: no runner lease' holds only when both lease names are absent (bin/dice:981-984). With one name set and the other absent the daemon rejects the request (bin/dice:987-988).

changes.name: DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID
changes.was: When either lease variable is set, the daemon rejects the request unless both are set, `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`, the pair matches a live process of the same user, and the client descends from that process. Do not set it by hand.
changes.now: When either lease variable is set, the daemon rejects the request unless both are integers, `DICE_LSF_RUNNING` is `1`, the pair matches a live process of the same user, and the client descends from that process. `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1` without the two lease variables is also rejected.
changes.why: Two rejections were missing: text that is not an integer (bin/dice:989-993) and DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1 with no lease (bin/dice:982-983). 'Do not set it by hand' was removed to make room: the listed conditions already show that a hand-set value is rejected.

changes.was: `dice` daemon, from the environment that a client sends with a submit request (`bin/dice`)
changes.now: `dice` daemon (`bin/dice`). It takes the name from the environment that a client sends with a submit request, not from its own environment.
changes.why: Same fact, in the read_by format (program, then file). The lookup is in the `env` field of the submit request (bin/dice:2963, bin/dice:2977-2981).

changes.name: DICE_LSF_LEASE_START_JIFFIES
changes.was: Unset: the submission has no runner lease. Empty: the daemon rejects the submit request.
changes.now: Unset: with `DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID` also unset, the submission has no runner lease. Empty: the daemon rejects the submit request.
changes.why: 'Unset: no runner lease' holds only when both lease names are absent (bin/dice:981-984). With one name set and the other absent the daemon rejects the request (bin/dice:987-988).

changes.name: DICE_LSF_LEASE_START_JIFFIES
changes.was: The daemon rejects a request that sets only one lease variable, or sets them without `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1`. A value of 0 clock ticks or less never matches a live process. The runner sets both variables only after it has read its own start time.
changes.now: The daemon rejects a request with only one lease variable, with text that is not an integer, or without `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1`. A value of 0 clock ticks or less never matches a live process. The runner sets both only after it reads its own start time.
changes.why: The rejection of text that is not an integer was missing (bin/dice:989-993).
